The biggest risk is that loss-making European acquisitions and the move into an unrelated business dilute returns on capital before the core device business can absorb them, and I cannot confirm the current earnings trend without the extracted results.

Rainbow Childrens Medicare runs a specialist chain of children's and women's hospitals: 26 hospitals with 1,910 operational beds out of 2,555 in total. About 65% of revenue comes from paediatrics, 63% of patients pay cash, and mature hospitals earn 73% of revenue at an ARPOB of about ₹66,900. In Q2FY27 revenue rose 23.2% YoY to ₹548 cr, up from +6.5% in Q2FY26 and +11.9% in Q3FY26, but PAT grew only about 11% to ₹84 cr. PAT margin has fallen from 17.0% to 15.3% and EBITDA margin from 33.5% to 31.0%, because the 5 new hospitals (12% of beds, 27.4% occupancy, -16% EBITDA margin) are still losing money and pulling the group's 49.2% occupancy down. For a capital-intensive hospital business I used EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick: at 26.1x it is only 12% above the broad-market median (P59) and within the usual range for Indian hospital chains, so valuation looks fair. Trailing P/E of 51.3x and P/B of 8.9x are rich, while a forward P/E of 36.5x assumes earnings growth. The biggest risk is that sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 3.6% over 30 days and 4.3% over 90 days even though all 14 analysts rate it a buy, which suggests margin dilution from new hospitals may last longer than the market expects.

fundamental.thesis: Indiamart runs a large Indian B2B online marketplace, with 8.9 million supplier storefronts and 217 thousand paying suppliers, and earns mainly from advance-paid supplier subscriptions, which makes it a platform rather than a typical consumer company. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-heavy hotel owner, the stock trades at 16.1x, 31% below the broad-market median (P29); trailing P/E is 39x and forward P/E is 22x. Near its 52-week low, that makes it fair to slightly cheap, but the leverage, the pending restructuring and steady small cuts to sell-side estimates (FY EPS -2% over 90 days) argue against a strong call.

fundamental.thesis: Swiggy is India's number-two food-delivery and quick-commerce (Instamart) platform, with a small but fast-growing out-of-home dining segment. Revenue keeps growing in the mid-30s: H1 FY27 rose 36.7% to ₹14,383 cr, and the implied Q2 is about ₹7,571 cr, up roughly 36% YoY, slower than FY26's +51.4%. Tenneco Clean Air India makes exhaust after-treatment and emission-control systems for Indian passenger-vehicle and commercial-vehicle makers, so it gains from tighter emission rules and richer vehicle mix. In the latest quarter with full numbers (Q1 FY27), revenue grew 20.2% YoY to ₹1,545 cr, up from 10.5% growth for FY26, but PAT fell 1.7% YoY to ₹165 cr and PAT margin slipped to 10.7% from 11.2% in FY26. H1 FY27 PAT of ₹339 cr implies Q2 FY27 PAT of about ₹174 cr, but the Q2 revenue figures filed on 2026-11-04 are not yet in the extracted data. Judged on P/E against auto-component peers, a trailing P/E of 38.2x is above the 18–28x sector range, so the stock is expensive on trailing earnings. The forward P/E of 27.7x and EV/EBITDA of 24.3x (in line with the broad-market median, P53) are less stretched. The main risks are faster sales growth not turning into profit growth, and analysts cutting next-year EPS estimates by 4.0% over 90 days even while 6 of 7 rate the stock a buy.

fundamental.thesis: Ola Electric makes electric two-wheelers and is building its own cell business; it has lost market share in a segment where the sector card says e-2W penetration is still rising (~6.5%), so its weakness is company-specific rather than an industry slump. fundamental.thesis: Balrampur Chini is one of India's largest integrated sugar makers: 80,000 TCD crushing, 1,050 KLPD distillery for ethanol, 175.7 MW saleable co-generation, and a new 80,000 TPA PLA bioplastics plant. That makes it a regulated, seasonal, capital-intensive commodity business rather than a true FMCG compounder, so the FMCG sector card and its 40-65x P/E norms do not fit here. In Q2FY27 revenue grew +12.3% YoY to ₹1,876 cr and PAT rose +81.6% to ₹104 cr (5.5% margin). That rebound follows a weak Q1FY27 (+6.1% revenue, PAT -14.4%), and H1FY27 shows revenue +9.3% and PAT +38.9%, but revenue growth has slowed from the +18-22% pace of FY26 and the Q2 EBITDA margin of 9.1% is below the FY26 full-year 13.0% (seasonal, but worth watching). Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this capital-intensive business, 25.0x and a trailing P/E of 38.0x look rich against the 12-22x Materials-style range. The forward P/E of 18.5x, sell-side FY EPS estimates raised +18.7% over 30 days and +29.4% over 90 days, and a P/B of 3.4x (P38 vs the broad market) pull the overall verdict back to fair, with the stock already at 77% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is government policy on sugar export quotas, minimum sale price, and ethanol procurement pricing, together with negative free cash flow (FY26 FCF -₹349 cr) from PLA and distillery capex, which together could leave the forward earnings that justify the multiple undelivered.

UNO Minda makes auto components for Indian OEMs, including lighting, switches, alloy wheels, acoustics, sunroofs and EV parts. It is a domestic-focused ancillary that benefits from premiumisation and the shift to EVs, and it announced a sunroof capacity expansion with its results. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27.2% YoY to ₹8,937 cr and PAT rose 19.7% to ₹756 cr, an 8.5% PAT margin. The Q2 press release reports record growth of 38% YoY in both revenue and PAT, so momentum is speeding up from the roughly 18-20% growth seen in FY26 and Q3 FY26. Cash backing is good: FY26 operating cash flow was 1.44x PAT. The quarter-by-quarter split in the trend table does not add up, though (the Q1 row of ₹5,557 cr cannot be reconciled with H1), and EBITDA margin slipped from 12.6% to 11.2%. Valuation is expensive: P/E is 53x trailing and 35.5x forward against an Auto-ancillary median of 18-28x, EV/EBITDA is 29x and P/B is 10x on a 19% ROE. All of these sit at the 64th-82nd percentile of the broad market, and the mean analyst target is only 2.4% above the price, even though analysts have raised EPS estimates by about 6% over the past 90 days. The main risk is that minority shareholders in subsidiaries take a growing share of profit: EPS grew only 3.6% against 19.7% PAT growth, which leaves little room for any slowdown after the festive season at this multiple.

fundamental.thesis: Affle 3i is a mobile ad-tech platform that sells cost-per-converted-user (CPCU) advertising, mainly in India and emerging markets; it is a platform business, not a headcount-based IT services firm. Growth is steady but not speeding up. H1 FY27 revenue rose 20.8% YoY to ₹1,531 cr and PAT rose 19.5% to ₹258 cr. Subtracting Q1 from H1 gives Q2 FY27 revenue of about ₹784 cr (around +21% YoY) and PAT of about ₹130 cr (about 16.6% margin), so YoY growth has held in a tight 19–21% band for six periods with PAT margin flat at 16.6–17.2%. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA (31.6x) plus forward P/E (29.7x), not the static IT-services P/E table, because Affle is a platform business. Trailing P/E of 46x is above the 22–30x IT range and about 31% above the broad-market median (P66). Forward P/E is at the top of that range, and the stock sits at 25.5% of its 52-week range. For a business growing about 20% with a ₹1,752 cr net cash cushion, I grade it fair, not cheap. Several things just added risk. The company agreed to acquire Israel-listed Perion Network, cancelled its earnings call citing a 'material development', and still has a ₹1,358 cr Bobble investment caught in insolvency, with a Supreme Court hearing on 25 Nov 2026. Cash conversion has also weakened to 0.65x CFO/PAT in H1.

fundamental.thesis: Cyient is a mid-cap engineering-services firm with three businesses: design and engineering services (DET, about 74% of revenue), electronics contract manufacturing (DLM), and a loss-making semiconductor unit, and it recently bought TAO Digital for about ₹2,156 cr. H1 FY27 revenue grew 23.4% YoY to ₹4,311 cr, but that growth is largely acquisition-driven, and PAT fell 19.7% YoY to ₹241 cr, so the PAT margin dropped from 8.6% to 5.6%. Profit has now fallen in every reported period (-24.9% in Q3FY26, -32.3% in Q1FY27, -19.7% in H1FY27), and the semiconductor unit lost ₹58 cr at a -16.5% margin. On valuation, I used P/E and EV/EBITDA together, and the stock looks fair rather than cheap: trailing P/E of 22.6x sits at the bottom of the 22–30x IT range, and EV/EBITDA of 11.4x ranks P16 against the broad market, but ROE is only 7.8%. The low 11.9x forward P/E rests on analyst estimates that were cut 18% over the last 90 days, so it should not be trusted yet. The biggest risk is that semiconductor losses and integrating TAO keep eating into the steady DET profits, and the data has gaps: the yfinance Q2 revenue of ₹1,498 cr conflicts with the filings, Q1FY27 shows two different growth rates, and the reported debt/equity and dividend-yield figures look like data errors.

Travel Food Services runs airport food and beverage outlets and lounges in India, operating at 22 airports with about 541 outlets, and has net cash of ₹451.5 cr with no traditional debt. In H1FY27, consolidated revenue rose 20.1% YoY to ₹878 cr and PAT rose 43.1% YoY to ₹276 cr. The Q1FY27 rate of +20.6% implies Q2 revenue of about ₹426 cr (+~20%) and PAT of about ₹147 cr, so growth is holding steady and PAT margin widened to 31.4% from 26.4%, with strong cash backing (CFO/PAT 1.57x). Much of that growth comes from new outlets (23 added in Q1) rather than existing ones: same-store sales grew only 4.2% while passenger traffic is falling. I used EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this concession-based business: at 23.3x it sits exactly at the broad-market median (P50), trailing P/E of 34.8x is also at the median and far below the 60–100x multiples typical of premium consumer names, and forward P/E of 29.5x implies further earnings growth, so with the stock mid-way through its 52-week range the grade is fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is the Delhi Terminal 3 subsidiary (60% owned and material to the group): its licence expired on 30 Sept 2026, and losing or re-pricing that concession would hit both revenue and margins.

fundamental.thesis: Intellect Design Arena is a mid-cap banking and insurance software maker. It sells licences, platform subscriptions and maintenance (AMC) to more than 500 financial institutions in 62 countries. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹855 cr, up 13.0% YoY, and growth has slowed over the trend window from +36.2% (Q2 FY26) to +20.6% (Q1FY27) to +13.0%. PAT was ₹104 cr, up only 1.8% YoY, and the PAT margin fell to 12.2% from 13.5% a year ago. EBITDA margin was 23.2% vs 24.3% a year ago, while LTM EBITDA margin fell about 344 bps to 22.4%, and LTM PBT is down 6.2%; management puts over ₹100 cr of that on AI investment. On the main IT yardstick, trailing P/E is 31.2×, just above the 22–30× sector range. The forward P/E of 18.4× and EV/EBITDA of 17.0× sit well below the broad-market median (P31–P43), so I grade it fair rather than cheap. The forward P/E leans on earnings growth that analysts are now cutting: FY EPS estimates are down about 10% and next-year estimates about 13% over 30–90 days. The biggest risk is that the heavy AI spending (the MSOCK platform) keeps squeezing margins while revenue growth keeps slowing, so revenue growth stops turning into profit growth.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% share of recent transmission bids, 29,802 circuit km of lines, a Mumbai distribution business, a fast-growing smart-meter business and a newly consolidated energy-trading platform. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr, a 13.1% PAT margin, after Q1 FY27 grew revenue 42.4% and PAT 124%. Two caveats apply to that growth: the H1 figures restate prior periods to include the energy-trading platform, and they count ₹4,961 cr of construction revenue (SCA, up from ₹3,692 cr). The extracted H1 rows also conflict (₹14,351 cr vs ₹19,787 cr). We grade valuation on EV/EBITDA plus P/B against ROE, the yardstick for capital-intensive utilities: EV/EBITDA of 25.1x, P/B of 7.2x on a 9.7% ROE and trailing P/E of 81.7x are far above the 10–18x utilities range, and the stock sits at 89.5% of its 52-week range. Analysts raising FY EPS estimates by about 16% in 30 days and a ₹87,222 cr transmission order book give good visibility, but the price already assumes flawless delivery. The main risks are leverage and execution: debt/equity is 1.84x, net debt is ₹41,067 cr, free cash flow is negative (₹-3,185 cr in H1), capex guidance is ₹21,000–25,000 cr a year, and Adani group news can move the stock regardless of results.

fundamental.thesis: NHPC is India's largest hydropower company, a state-owned utility that earns a regulated return on the plants it commissions, so its profits grow as new capacity comes online (Subansiri Lower is now at 1,250 MW of a planned 2,000 MW). In H1 FY27 revenue rose 26.0% YoY to Rs 8,291 cr and PAT rose 20.6% to Rs 2,836 cr, a 34.2% margin, up from +14.5% and +8.6% in H1 FY26. However, Rs 918 cr of that revenue is provisional Parbati-II income still awaiting CERC tariff approval, and without it revenue growth is closer to +12%. The trend table mixes half-year, nine-month and full-year periods, so only the H1-vs-H1 comparison is reliable. On valuation (using EV/EBITDA and P/E against the utilities benchmark), EV/EBITDA of 25.5x and trailing P/E of 27.4x are well above the 10-18x utility P/E band, and P/B of 1.85x is rich for a 9% ROE, so the stock looks expensive even though it sits low (24%) in its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that debt-funded capex is outpacing earnings: finance costs more than doubled (+115%), net debt is Rs 56,674 cr, and consensus FY EPS has been cut 20% in 30 days.

fundamental.thesis: Anant Raj is an NCR-focused mid-cap developer that is building a data-centre and cloud business alongside its residential projects; a Board-approved demerger of the data-centre arm into a subsidiary is awaiting NCLT approval. Growth has slowed sharply: H1 FY27 revenue was ₹1,293 cr (+5.7% YoY), down from +24-26% through FY26, and the implied Q2 FY27 revenue of about ₹662 cr was only about +5% YoY. PAT still grew faster than revenue, reaching ₹306 cr (+15.8%), because EBITDA margin widened to 32.3% from about 27-29%. On the sector card's yardstick valuation looks fair: P/E is not meaningful for developers and pre-sales/bookings data was not provided, so I graded on P/B 3.2x against an annualised ROE of about 10-11% (a rich pairing) and EV/EBITDA 28.6x (P63 vs the broad market), offset by a forward P/E of 18.5x and P/B at P36. The biggest risk is weak cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was only about ₹32 cr against ₹306 cr of PAT (0.10x), and FY26 free cash flow was -₹693 cr, so reported profits are not yet turning into cash while capex and inventory of about ₹1,507 cr keep rising.

Bharti Hexacom is Bharti Airtel's listed subsidiary covering the Rajasthan and North-East telecom circles, with about 30 million customers. Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹2,582 cr, up 11.4% YoY, a slight pick-up from 10.9% in Q1 and 9.4% for FY26. PAT was ₹566 cr, up 34.4%, with PAT margin widening to 21.9% from 19.2% in Q1. EBITDAaL rose 14.2%, cash generation is strong (FY26 CFO/PAT of 2.6x) and net debt is low at 0.31x EBITDAaL. The weak spot is ARPU, the sector's key number: it grew only 5.2% to ₹264, which suggests growth is coming more from data usage and broadband than from pricing power. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card names. At 15.4x it is well above the 9-12x norm for Indian mobile, and a trailing P/E of 41x is also expensive. A forward P/E of 22x already assumes a lot of earnings growth, while analysts have cut EPS estimates 2-3% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that the next tariff hike gets delayed while estimates keep falling, which could push the multiple down even with the stock near its 52-week low.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Power is an integrated utility spanning power generation (thermal plus a fast-growing renewables arm), transmission, distribution and solar manufacturing/EPC, so it is not a pure regulated annuity like NTPC or POWERGRID. Revenue growth has picked up over three quarters, from +1.0% (Q3FY26) to +5.6% (Q1FY27) to +26.3% in Q2FY27 at ₹19,636 cr, with PAT up 32.6% YoY to ₹1,652 cr (8.4% margin, up from 7.4% in Q1); the ₹59 cr exceptional gain is too small to change the picture, and sell-side FY EPS estimates were raised 5.4% over the last 30 days. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-heavy utility, plus P/B against ROE: EV/EBITDA is 15.2x, trailing P/E is 34.4x (well above the 10-18x utilities benchmark) and P/B is 3.3x on only 11.3% ROE, all richer than regulated peers that earn about 15.5% ROE. It looks fair only against the broad market (P48 on P/E), so we grade it expensive for its sector, and the 23.6x forward P/E already prices in strong growth. The biggest risk is the balance sheet: debt/equity is 1.62x, interest coverage only 2.48x, the current ratio 0.79x, and H1 free cash flow was negative at ₹-3,696 cr, so returns depend on renewables capex being commissioned on time while borrowing costs stay high (US 10Y at 5.11%, unclear RBI direction).

fundamental.thesis: Vodafone Idea is the weakest of India's three private telecom operators, with about 194 million subscribers, and it is losing ground to Jio and Airtel in a market where prices are being steadily raised. In Q2FY27 revenue grew 6.2% YoY to ₹11,884 cr, up from +1.9% in Q3FY26 and +6.0% in Q1FY27, and customer ARPU rose 9.7% YoY to ₹198 (from ₹186 in Q3FY26 and ₹195 in Q1FY27). Profits are still deeply negative, though: H1FY27 net loss was ₹9,729 cr, so Q2 alone lost about ₹5,975 cr (about -50% of revenue). That is worse than Q1's -₹3,754 cr loss, partly because of a ₹462 cr one-off charge, and finance costs of ₹5,351 cr eat up roughly 45% of revenue. We graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for telecom. At 28.6x it is far above the card's 9–12x range for Indian mobile operators and at the 63rd percentile of the broad market, so the stock is expensive. The 4.3x trailing P/E is not meaningful because it is inflated by a one-off FY26 accounting gain (FY26 PAT of ₹34,552 cr was larger than the business can earn), and with negative net worth the P/B figure is not meaningful either. The stock sits at 90% of its 52-week range, the average analyst target is about 4% below the current price, and 18 of 22 analysts rate it hold or sell, so the risk/reward from here looks poor.

fundamental.thesis: L&T Finance is a large retail-focused NBFC (₹1.32 lakh crore loan book) under the L&T Group umbrella, operating across rural/farm finance, two-wheelers, housing, and consumer lending segments with strong parentage and a well-capitalised balance sheet (CAR 18.67%). Revenue growth has sharply accelerated from +10.1% in H1FY26 to +24.4% in H1FY27, with PAT rising +31.6% YoY to ₹1,889 cr and PAT margins expanding from 16.5% to 17.6%; critically, the primary NBFC KPIs are moving in the right direction — Gross NPA has improved consistently from 3.19% to 2.75% over four periods, Net NPA from 0.96% to 0.85%, and ROA has risen to 2.39% from 2.27% in FY26, confirming this is not just revenue-led growth. Using P/B+ROE as the mandated NBFC yardstick (not P/E), LTF at 2.76× P/B with rising ROA ranks at P30 vs broad-market peers on both P/E and P/B (below sector median by 30–40%), and its trailing P/E of 24.57× sits within the 18–28× NBFC benchmark range while a forward P/E of 15.83× — a 36% discount to trailing — prices in strong near-term earnings growth, placing it at fair value with a modest cheap lean. The primary risk is that impairment provisions grew 15.6% YoY and credit cost remained elevated at 11.29% of total income, sell-side next-FY EPS estimates have been trimmed -3.2% over 30 days, and the highly leveraged balance sheet (D/E 393×) leaves LTF exposed to any funding-market stress or a slower-than-expected credit cost normalisation.

MCX runs India's main commodity derivatives exchange and has a near-monopoly in exchange-traded commodity futures and options; in FY26 it added electricity futures and cardamom futures and strengthened gold and silver spot-price discovery. Q2 FY27 results were filed on 2026-11-03 and the earnings call was held on 2026-11-04, but the trend table has no extracted revenue or PAT figures for any period, so we cannot say whether growth is speeding up or slowing down. MCX is an exchange, not a lender, so it is judged on P/E and EV/EBITDA rather than bank-style P/B. On that basis it trades at 53.9x trailing earnings (P73 against broad-market peers, 53% above the 35.2x median) and 39.3x EV/EBITDA (P81). The forward P/E of 33.6x shows strong earnings growth is already priced in. A P/B of 17x is supported by a 37.9% ROE and almost no debt (debt/equity 0.11). Overall the stock is fair to stretched rather than cheap, with the price about 1% above the mean analyst target of ₹3,674. The main risk is that exchange volumes are cyclical and the business is exposed to regulatory or fee changes, and at this multiple the stock has little room to absorb any slowdown in trading activity.

fundamental.thesis: Brainbees (FirstCry) is India's largest multi-channel retailer of baby and kids products, with an online platform, about 1,000+ offline stores, the GlobalBees house of brands and a growing preschool business. The filings table shows Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹2,106 cr, up 13.0% YoY, with India multi-channel up 18% and offline same-store growth of 15%, but the inputs conflict: the filings table shows PAT of ₹51 cr while yfinance shows ₹1,337 cr revenue and a ₹31 cr loss for the same quarter, the H1FY26 row (₹396 cr revenue) is clearly wrong, and EBITDA margin has slipped from 5.0% to 4.6% to 4.2%, with adjusted EBITDA flat despite double-digit growth. Trailing P/E is not meaningful for this barely profitable platform-retailer, so I graded on EV/sales and unit economics: price/sales of 1.24x and P/B of 2.2x (P22 vs the broad market) are undemanding for Consumer Discretionary, but EV/EBITDA of 159x (P100) and forward P/E of 49x show the market is paying for a margin recovery that has not shown up yet, so I grade it fair, with the stock near its 52-week low. The biggest risk is tomorrow's Q2FY27 result (board meeting on 14 Nov 2026): management promised to win back 260 bps of gross margin by Q2-Q3, and if that slips while diapering competition from quick-commerce stays intense, it could reset expectations sharply.

fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. It is tagged IT here, but its demand comes from US healthcare operations, not tech spending. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,032 cr, up 22.5% YoY, and PAT was ₹284 cr, up 13.3%. Growth has slowed from +35.7% (Q3FY26) to +29.1% (FY26) to +25.0% (H1) to +22.5%, and constant-currency growth is only about 12%, so roughly half the headline growth comes from the weak rupee. Reported PAT margin fell to 14.0% from 15.1% a year ago, and adjusted PAT grew only 8.1% even though adjusted EBITDA margin reached a six-quarter high of 26.3%. On valuation, using P/E and EV/EBITDA, the trailing P/E of 21.5x is below the IT sector's 22–30x range and sits at about the 24th percentile of the broad market (there are no close peers in the universe). EV/EBITDA is 11.4x, forward P/E is 15.4x, and cash conversion is strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x), so the stock looks cheap. The biggest risk is client concentration: the top 3 clients are 60% of revenue and the top 10 are 84%, and voluntary attrition is high at 25.7%. Losing or repricing a single large client could hurt badly. The yfinance dividend yield (44%) and debt/equity (11.5) figures look like unit errors, so I ignored them.

ITI is a government-owned telecom and defence equipment maker that has been under a long-running government revival plan; the Telecom sector card is written for mobile operators and doesn't fit this business, so I relied on the filings instead. In Q1FY27, revenue fell 14.6% YoY to Rs 425 cr from Rs 498 cr and the company lost Rs 32 cr, which is a smaller loss than Rs 64 cr a year ago. The PAT margin improved from -12.8% to about -7.6%, but it is still negative, and the large defence order book is still not turning into billed revenue (the reported order-book number has an obvious unit error, so I did not use it). On valuation, the 79x trailing P/E is misleading because FY26 profit comes from a one-off Rs 449 cr restructuring gain; stripping it out leaves an underlying loss, so I graded on EV/EBITDA, which is 483x against a 9-12x telecom norm and sits around the 87th-90th percentile of the market on P/E and P/B, so it is clearly expensive. The biggest risk is earnings quality: the auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion over revenue recognition and internal controls, and receivables from government customers that are more than 3 years overdue are barely provided for. The Q2FY27 results filed today were not in the data I had, which caps conviction.

PAT margin has contracted from 25.2% a year ago to 20.8%, and from 24.1% for FY26. The main cause is mix: digital services (H1 revenue ₹793 cr, +50% YoY) earns a 6.2% segment margin against 39.7% in visa, and acquisition costs from Atyati and the Trefeddian hotel add to the pressure. On valuation, using EV/EBITDA and P/E together with cash conversion, the stock looks cheap: trailing P/E is 13.8x and EV/EBITDA is 10.2x, both around the 11th percentile of the broad market (median 35.2x / 23.3x). The biggest risk is that the shift toward digital services keeps diluting margins, so strong revenue growth fails to turn into earnings growth.

Vardhman Textiles is one of India's largest integrated textile makers, selling yarn, fabric and acrylic fibre. It is a cyclical, commodity-linked business and does not belong with the premium consumer franchises in its yfinance sector tag. Growth has picked up sharply: revenue growth rose from about +1% in FY26 to +13.3% in Q1 FY27 and about +15.6% in Q2 FY27. Q2 FY27 is derived as H1 minus Q1: revenue ₹2,866 cr and PAT ₹358 cr. Q2 PAT nearly doubled from ₹187 cr a year ago, and EBITDA margin jumped from 13.4% in FY26 to 21.5% in H1, with strong cash backing (CFO/PAT 1.48x, FCF ₹468 cr). Because the business is capital-intensive, valuation was graded on EV/EBITDA: at 15.2x it sits 35% below the market median, trailing P/E is 25.3x and forward P/E is 14.6x. That is offset by P/B of 1.85x on a weak 7.3% ROE and a price at 98% of its 52-week range, so the stock is fair rather than cheap. The biggest risk is that the margin jump is a cyclical peak driven by raw-material spreads rather than a lasting shift; next-year EPS estimates are already being trimmed (-2.5% over 30 days) and the sell-side mix leans hold/sell.

Emami is a mid-sized FMCG company selling Ayurvedic personal-care and OTC health brands (Navratna, BoroPlus, Zandu, Kesh King), with about 85% of revenue from India; it has recently bought Axiom Ayurveda (73.5% stake, from April 2026) and IncNut Digital (60%, from June 2026). In H1 FY27, consolidated revenue rose 24.9% YoY to ₹2,127 cr, a sharp turnaround from -0.8% in FY26, but much of this jump comes from the two acquisitions, and exports fell 3.9%. PAT fell 9.0% to ₹284 cr, and PAT margin compressed from 17.9% to 13.1% (EBITDA margin 25.6% → 22.6%) as acquisition costs and finance charges (₹5.1 cr → ₹11.7 cr) hit profits, so growth is being bought, not earned organically, and the filings give no volume-growth figure to check real demand. On P/E plus EV/EBITDA, the stock looks cheap: trailing P/E of 22.5× and forward P/E of 18.5× are far below the 40–65× FMCG norm, EV/EBITDA is 17.7× (24% below the broad-market median), it trades at only 9% of its 52-week range, and ROE is 27.6% with a net-cash balance sheet (₹78 cr); however, the sector card warns that cheap FMCG usually signals a structural problem, and sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 2.8–3.0% over 30–90 days. The biggest risk is that the acquired businesses keep diluting margins while the core franchise shows little organic volume growth, which would justify the de-rating rather than reverse it.

However, H1 PAT fell 35.7% to ₹328 cr, implied Q2 PAT was only about ₹135 cr (4.9% margin, 11.2% EBITDA margin), and EBITDA margin has slid every period from 20.3% to 12.7%. The ₹17 cr 3EV impairment explains only a small part of that fall, so the squeeze is mainly gas costs. On valuation, the business is closest to a regulated utility, so I graded it on EV/EBITDA plus P/E: trailing P/E of 14.2x sits inside the 10–18x utilities band and EV/EBITDA is 7.4x. Sentiment is neutral and stale, with no fresh news and money flowing out of the Utilities sector. fundamental.thesis: SJVN is a government-owned regulated hydropower IPP (flagship 1,500 MW Nathpa Jhakri complex) expanding aggressively into renewables and thermal (Buxar 1,320 MW), earning a CERC-regulated ROE on commissioned capacity — earnings growth is therefore a function of commissioning pace, not power prices. Q1FY27 revenue surged +52% YoY to ₹1,394 cr driven by capacity additions, but PAT fell 1.2% to ₹225 cr as PAT margin compressed severely from 24.8% to 16.1% — a pattern that has deteriorated every quarter for six periods, with EBITDA margin also contracting from ~88% to 66%, reflecting rising interest burden on a highly leveraged balance sheet (D/E 2.25×, DSCR 0.60 — a 40% shortfall in debt servicing). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for a capital-intensive regulated utility, at 15.88× SJVN sits within the regulated-utility peer range and at P28 vs broad market, while P/B at 1.86× (P16 vs peers) and forward P/E at 14× (P22 vs peers, deep discount to trailing 38×) reflect market pricing in earnings recovery — grading overall as fair, but the 52-week position at 12.8% of range and ongoing sell-side EPS cuts of -13.3% over 30 days caution against treating the cheapness as a catalyst. The DSCR of 0.60 combined with a current ratio of 0.54 means near-term liquidity is structurally stressed, and the NJHPS tariff determination pending since April 2024 (₹3,200+ cr billed provisionally under an expired 2019 tariff) creates a binary earnings event with no resolution timeline visible.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Total Gas is a city gas distributor selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas to homes and businesses, and it is still expanding, with 80-90 new CNG stations and 2+ lakh home connections targeted for FY27. The latest quarter with usable numbers is Q1FY27 because Q2FY27 results were filed on 22 Oct but are missing from the trend table: revenue rose 27.2% YoY to Rs 1,907 cr (up from +20.9% in Q1FY26), while PAT fell 14.2% to Rs 142 cr, PAT margin shrank from 11.0% to 7.4%, and EBITDA margin fell from 19.9% to 11.2%, so growth is becoming less profitable. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock is expensive at 58.9x versus a 23.3x broad-market median (P93), and its 105.3x trailing P/E (P94) and 13.4x P/B (P91) agree, though this is a broad-market comparison because no close peers are available, and the 4.0% dividend yield looks unreliable against this P/E so I give it no weight. The biggest risk is that margins do not recover as management expects from long-term gas contracts and lower costs, leaving a very high multiple resting on shrinking profit, and the missing Q2FY27 numbers could confirm or challenge this view.

The biggest risk is that growth and margins disappoint together, as management expects H2 industry growth of only mid to high single digits (low single digits for petrol models) amid commodity inflation, and the standalone EBITDA margin of 13.3% is still below the 14-16% target corridor.

Bajaj Holdings is a near-debt-free holding company: its earnings come from dividends, interest and its share of profits from its large stakes in Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv, so revenue (₹576 cr in H1FY27) is a small figure next to profit. Reported H1FY27 PAT fell 6.7% YoY to ₹4,845 cr and revenue fell 20.1%, but that is mainly because last year included a one-off ₹1,522 cr gain from selling Bajaj Finserv shares. Without that gain, PAT rose about 37%, and the share of associate profits grew 32% to ₹4,626 cr, helped by Bajaj Auto Q2 PAT up 62% and Bajaj Finserv up 23%. Reported growth has slowed sharply, from +65.6% to -6.7% half-year on half-year, but the underlying associate engine is accelerating. Using the holding-company yardstick (discount to NAV, not P/E or EV/EBITDA, which mean little here), the stock trades at about a 52% discount to the reported NAV of ₹21,578 per share (estimated price around ₹10,300). That sits in the middle of the usual 40–60% holdco discount band, and peer P/E of 11.4x (P33) and P/B of 1.5x with ROE of 12.6% back a 'fair' grade, with the stock in the lower third of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is concentration: value depends almost entirely on Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv share prices, and the holdco discount may not narrow, so this is a leveraged-looking proxy on two group stocks rather than an independent earnings story.

fundamental.thesis: Solar Industries makes commercial explosives for coal miners such as CIL and SCCL, and it is now growing fast as a defence ammunition and energetics supplier. It sits under the Materials label, but it is really an explosives and defence business, so steel and chemical multiples do not apply. In the half-year to September 2026 (HY27, from the official filing), revenue grew +69.7% YoY to ₹7,187 cr and PAT grew +84.3% to ₹1,316 cr. That is faster than FY26 (+30.0% revenue) and Q3FY26 (+29.0%), and defence revenue more than doubled (+109% to ₹1,935 cr). EBITDA margin widened about 140 bps to 28.4%, so the pre-computed 'contracting' margin flag looks like a period-ordering artefact. The ₹20,178 cr order book (87% defence) covers roughly 2 years of revenue. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive business. At 65.8x EV/EBITDA, 101.7x trailing P/E and 32x P/B, the stock is at P93–P99 versus the broad market, well above the 12–22x Materials range and rich even for a defence name. The forward P/E of 63x and estimate upgrades (+11% FY-EPS over 90 days) show strong growth is already priced in, and the price is at 97% of its 52-week range. So: expensive. The biggest risk is that the defence order flow is lumpy and largely export-driven, so any slip in orders or execution would hit a stock priced for perfection.

fundamental.thesis: NTPC is India's largest power generator. Most of its earnings come from a regulated return (about 15.5% ROE) on the plants it has commissioned, with a fast-growing solar and renewables arm on top. H1 FY27 headline revenue was ₹100,262 cr, up 19.9% from ₹83,660 cr a year ago, but the company's core capacity-plus-energy billing grew a more modest 9.65%. Within that, capacity charges rose 6.7% to ₹35,909 cr, energy charges rose 11.6% to ₹55,845 cr and solar revenue rose 64.9% to ₹2,456 cr. Revenue growth has turned up from about -1.5% to -3% in FY26 to +7.0% in Q1 FY27 (PAT ₹6,896 cr, +12.9%, 13.6% margin), though H1 PAT was not extracted. For a capital-intensive utility I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, backed by P/B with ROE. On that basis it looks cheap against peers: EV/EBITDA is 8.4x against a peer median of 11.6x (cheapest in the peer group) and trailing P/E is 11.9x against 14.7x. P/B is 1.7x with ROE of 13.7%. It is only fair against the static 10–18x utilities P/E band. The forward P/E (12.8x) is above the trailing P/E, and this year's EPS estimates were trimmed 0.9% in the last 30 days, so near-term earnings look roughly flat. The main risk is earnings quality: CERC 2024 tariff orders are still pending, so bills are provisional and later adjusted (₹2,825 cr energy adjustment in H1), and large regulatory-deferral and deferred-tax swings make reported PAT hard to compare across periods.

That risk is larger because, in a risk-off market, a stock priced for perfection can lose 30-50% of its valuation multiple quickly.

Earnings are recovering sharply from last year's microfinance stress: Q2 FY27 PAT, derived as H1 ₹995 cr minus Q1 ₹493 cr, is about ₹502 cr on total income of about ₹1,904 cr. That is roughly 7-8x the year-ago quarter, but off a provisioning-hit base, so the +691% H1 PAT and +144% revenue figures overstate the underlying growth, and the revenue figure also mixes NII with total income across periods. Asset quality is the real story: GNPA improved from 4.04% (9M FY26) to 3.17% (FY26) to 2.18% (Q1 FY27), with collection efficiency at 97.4% and provision coverage holding around 65%. Using the sector card's P/B-vs-ROE yardstick for lenders, a P/B of 2.91x against a TTM ROE of 16.4% (annualised H1 ROE about 24%) looks fair rather than cheap. The low forward P/E of 11x simply reflects the earnings normalisation, and analysts have raised FY EPS estimates by 9.8% in the last 30 days. The main risks are a fresh stress cycle in unsecured rural lending, a borrower count that is shrinking (-2.4% YoY) even as loan size grows, and a risk-off macro backdrop for a leveraged midcap lender.

fundamental.thesis: Pine Labs is India's leading merchant commerce platform operating ~2.17 million POS/DCP devices with embedded affordability finance, UPI infrastructure, and an expanding international footprint (UAE, Malaysia) — a high-growth fintech rather than a traditional lender despite its Financials sector tag. Valuation is expensive on most yardsticks: trailing P/E of 147× sits at P98 vs peers and far above any sector benchmark (IT 22–30×, Financials 12–18×); EV/EBITDA of 25.7× is more moderate at P58, and forward P/E of 31.7× (P67) is reasonable IF the earnings ramp materialises, but ROE of only 2.4% with D/E of 7.47 makes the P/B of 2.9× difficult to defend — using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick per the sector card's platform guidance, 'fair-to-expensive' is the honest grade, leaning expensive given the ROE/leverage combination. The biggest near-term risk is that the effective tax rate of 48% (vs guided 28-30%) and persistent EBITDA margin compression prevent the PAT inflection on which the forward multiple entirely depends, exposing the stock — already at its 52-week low — to further de-rating.

fundamental.thesis: Jindal Saw is a midcap maker of large-diameter line pipe and ductile-iron pipe; it is tagged Industrials but trades on a materials and steel-pipe cycle, and no order-book or book-to-bill data was provided to check pipeline visibility. On EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a capital-intensive business, the stock looks cheap at 12.8x (P21, about 45% below the broad-market median), and P/B of 1.6x is also low. Trailing P/E of 30.5x sits inside the 28-45x Industrials band, so I grade valuation fair rather than cheap. That is because the stock is at 98.5% of its 52-week range while earnings are falling, and the 13.6x forward P/E depends on an earnings recovery that analysts cut by 23% in the last 30 days. The biggest risks are further margin decline and the ₹1,891 cr JITF arbitration case, which now goes to a third judge.

Syrma SGS is a mid-sized Indian electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company that builds products for about 270 customers, and it benefits from China+1 sourcing and the PLI scheme; exports are now 26% of operating revenue and grew 80-91% YoY in H1. Growth has sped up: H1 FY27 revenue was ₹3,603 cr (+70.9% YoY) and PAT was ₹230 cr (+97.7%), and the implied Q2 revenue of about ₹2,000 cr (+73% YoY) follows +67% in Q1 and +43% in Q3 FY26; however, EBITDA margin slipped to 10.2% in Q2 from 10.7% a year earlier, and the implied Q2 PAT margin is only about 6.2%. Trailing P/E of 79.7x (P87) is far above the 28-45x Industrials range, so the stock is expensive, though a forward P/E of 47x and steadily rising analyst estimates (next-FY EPS +7% over 90 days) show strong earnings growth is already expected. With the price at 99% of its 52-week range, the stock is priced for perfection, and any slowdown in growth or further margin squeeze from component shortages could trigger the 30-50% de-rating typical of this sector.

fundamental.thesis: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is a mid-cap pharma company that sells branded medicines in India (41% of revenue) and exports to Europe, Canada and other markets (59%); it sells little into the US, so the US tariff risk is low. Growth is speeding up: revenue growth went from +14.9% in H1 FY26 to +19.5% in FY26 and +24.8% in H1 FY27 (₹486 cr). Q2 FY27, worked out as H1 minus Q1, was about ₹255 cr (+26% YoY) with PAT of about ₹60 cr, and H1 PAT grew +37.5% while EBITDA margin rose 357 bps to 43.4% and cash conversion stayed strong (FY26 CFO/PAT 1.56x). The sector card has no diagnostics yardstick, so I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/E. The stock is expensive: trailing P/E of 82.8x against a healthcare band of 28–40x, EV/EBITDA of 41.9x, the 83rd–94th percentile of the broad market on every multiple, and a price at 90% of its 52-week range. The consensus target is only about 8% above the price, so most of the strong delivery already looks priced in. The biggest risk is that this rich multiple depends on new hubs in Bengaluru, Kolkata and the North-East ramping up on time, while finance costs rose 46% YoY and Hyderabad still dominates revenue.

fundamental.thesis: DOMS Industries is a leading Indian maker of branded stationery and art supplies, with a growing hygiene business; the desk files it under FMCG, while yfinance lists it as Industrials. fundamental.thesis: Chennai Petroleum is a standalone refiner and IOC subsidiary, so its earnings track gross refining margins (GRM, the profit per barrel of crude processed) rather than administered retail fuel prices.
