Growth is slowing: the latest filing shows revenue of ₹3,877 cr (+13.5% YoY) and PAT of ₹338 cr (+9.8%), down from +18.7% revenue growth in Q1 FY27 and +20.4% in FY26. EBITDA margin slipped from 14.75% to 14.23% YoY, and PAT growing slower than revenue points to cost pressure. Cash conversion is strong: CFO/PAT is 2.2x, FCF is ₹673 cr and net debt is a minimal ₹137 cr. On valuation I graded on EV/EBITDA and P/E against the sector card's 60-100x norm for premium consumer names. A trailing P/E of 65.9x (44.2x forward) and EV/EBITDA of 29.1x put it at the low end of that band, so fair. It is still not cheap for mid-teens growth: it sits at P81 on P/E in a broad-market peer set, because there are no tight retail peers in the universe. The biggest risk is that growth keeps slowing while the stock carries a premium multiple. Analysts are trimming EPS estimates (FY next -2% over 90 days) while 18 of 19 still rate it a buy, a pattern that often comes before a de-rating. The extracted H1 figures (₹3,877 cr) also look inconsistent with Q1 alone (₹3,727 cr), so treat the trajectory numbers with caution.

drivers: Latest results (filed 2026-10-29) drew an in-line reaction: +1.5% after 1 day, drifting to +3.4% after 2 days. A mild positive follow-through, but not a clear beat.

Management tone is very stale: the Q1FY26 filing is 474 days old and gave no forward guidance. Its strong figures (revenue +21.9% YoY, PAT +52.4% YoY, EBITDA margin up to 15.55%) and the widening JV loss are background only.
Auto sector shows institutional inflow (+2.06% vs benchmark over 5 days, 92% of stocks advancing), but yesterday's -0.98% suggests the momentum is fading.
News is a data gap: one headline matched, with no FinBERT score and no material company catalysts. Rising crude adds a mild headwind for Auto. Midcap liquidity argues for caution.

technical.setup: Sharp one-month bounce (+12.8%) has pushed price to the upper Bollinger band and just under the falling 200-day average. The 'breakout' label is unconfirmed because ADX is 19, below the 20 trend threshold, and the long-term structure is still a death cross with SMA50 below SMA200. Volume accumulation is supportive, but in a mean-reverting regime this extended move is not a buy.

trader.reasoning: We don't own this stock, and none of the three analysts makes a case for buying. The fundamental data is poor: the latest official filing is over a year old, and the low P/E rests on unverified recent earnings. Sentiment is neutral after an in-line results reaction, and the chart shows an extended bounce sitting just under a falling 200-day average with no confirmed trend. With the portfolio fully invested, the market in a mean-reverting phase, rising crude weighing on autos, and midcap liquidity risk, nothing here justifies selling another holding to fund an entry.

fundamental.thesis: Force Motors is a midcap Indian vehicle maker, but the data provided does not show its market share, product mix or EV position, so its competitive standing cannot be judged here. The latest extracted filing is Q1 FY26, when revenue was Rs 2,297 cr (+21.9% YoY, slower than +26.7% in Q1 FY25) and PAT was Rs 176 cr (+52.4%), with PAT margin rising from 6.1% to 7.7%; that data is over a year old, the 28 Oct 2026 results are not extracted, and the unverified yfinance Q2 FY27 figures (revenue Rs 2,090.69 cr, PAT Rs 293.88 cr, about 14% margin) cannot confirm the current trend, while the 9M and H1 rows mix cumulative periods and the H1 FY25 revenue of Rs 383 cr looks wrong. On the trailing P/E yardstick the card sets for auto makers, 19.15x sits at the low end of the 18-30x range, so I grade it fair, not cheap: EV/EBITDA of 14.95x and P/E at P20 look low only against a broad-market fallback group rather than true auto peers, P/B is 5.81x, the earnings behind the P/E are unverified, and the 29.0% dividend yield looks like a data error and is ignored. The biggest risk is that this low multiple rests on recent earnings that may include one-offs or peak margins, and neither the filings nor the unknown purpose of the two 26 Oct 2026 shareholder-class EGMs could be checked.

drivers: Negative earnings surprise: stock fell 4.2% the day after Q2FY27 results and 5.1% over two days, so the market was disappointed

Management reiterated guidance with no upgrade (3-4% Food & FMCG EBITDA margin, Rs 4,000-4,500/MT edible-oil EBITDA). Strong 32% Food & FMCG revenue growth was offset by PAT falling 2% YoY despite 26% revenue growth

Balance-sheet and demand concerns: H1 operating cash flow was negative because of a Rs 6,000 crore inventory build from the sunflower disruption, and rural demand is weak with a 30-40% rainfall deficit in wheat belts
No company headlines in the last 7 days (data gap). FMCG sector flow is neutral, and rising crude is a mild input-cost headwind

technical.setup: Range-bound drift lower inside a long-term downtrend: price sits below the 20, 50 and 200-day averages in a bearish stack, momentum is weak (RSI 37, MACD negative) and selling volume outweighs buying, but ADX at 18.4 shows no real trend and RSI is not yet oversold enough to signal a confirmed reversal.

trader.reasoning: We don't own AWL, and none of the three views makes a case to buy it. The fundamental view rates it fair value with moderate growth: revenue rose about 26%, but Q2 profit fell about 2% and the profit margin is only about 1%, so small input-cost moves can wipe out earnings. Sentiment is bearish after the stock fell on results, with negative operating cash flow and weak rural demand, while the chart is in a weak, trendless downtrend below all its moving averages with no reversal yet. With rising crude a headwind for this low-margin midcap and only about Rs 18,400 in cash, there is no reason to fund a position now; we would look again on a confirmed bounce off support near Rs 156 alongside proof that profits are catching up with sales.

fundamental.thesis: AWL Agri Business sells edible oils under the Fortune brand, along with packaged foods and industrial inputs such as oleochemicals, and reaches about 135 million households, but it earns thin margins typical of a commodity processor rather than a premium FMCG company. Revenue growth accelerated from +18% in Q1 to about +26% in Q2 (roughly Rs 22,202 cr, derived as H1 minus Q1), and H1 volume growth of 11% extends the improvement from 2-3% in Q2-Q3 FY26 and 7% in Q1 FY27, but Q2 PAT swung from +48% to about -2% YoY (Rs 239 cr vs Rs 245 cr), partly due to a Bangladesh minimum tax, while PAT margin fell from 1.8% to about 1.1%, so the 'expanding' margin signal in the trend table, which mixes half-year and quarterly periods, looks unreliable. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, the stock looks fair, leaning cheap, at 9.0x (P8) and 20.7x trailing P/E near its 52-week low, because the broad-market peer set and 40-65x FMCG norm are poor comparisons for a 3% EBITDA-margin business, and 2.29x book for an estimated 11% ROE is not a clear bargain; the 54% dividend yield and 10.62 debt/equity look like data errors (debt/equity is probably about 0.11x), and the +55.6% consensus upside looks overstated because the implied price is below the 52-week low. The biggest risk is that growth keeps failing to reach profit, since edible oil volumes grew only 5%, EBITDA of Rs 4,100/MT sits at the low end of the Rs 4,000-4,500 guidance, and small moves in input costs can have an outsized effect on a margin this thin.

drivers: Management reiterated (not raised) the FY27 target of 'INR 4,000 crores revenue' and '30–40% CAGR'. Record Q2 growth of 335.7% YoY is offset by gross-margin compression from '200%+ component price inflation' and a cash conversion cycle stretching to 94 days.
Earnings reaction was in-line: the stock moved -1.1% on both the 1-day and 2-day windows after results, so the market showed no strong approval of the record quarter.
IT sector headwind: strong institutional outflow, with the sector up +1.74% vs the benchmark's +5.67% over 5 days (-3.93% relative).
No ticker-specific headlines in the last 7 days, so no news confirms the outlook. For a midcap this data gap lowers conviction.

technical.setup: Breakdown in a strong downtrend: price sits about 8.5% below the 200-day average with MACD still falling and selling volume heavier than buying volume. RSI at 27 is oversold and could bounce, but nothing yet confirms a reversal, and the earlier golden-cross structure is fading.

trader.reasoning: Netweb's AI-server growth is strong, but the stock is expensive at about 109x trailing and 61x forward earnings. Margins are under pressure from component-cost inflation and a 94-day cash cycle, and the extracted H1 filing is OCR-corrupted, so the Q2 numbers can't be fully verified. Sentiment is neutral and the stock barely reacted to a record quarter. Technically it is in a downtrend about 8.5% below its 200-day average with MACD still falling; RSI at 27 is oversold, but there is no reversal confirmation, and the mean-reverting regime gate needs fundamental or sentiment support that isn't there. With no position, a midcap's lumpy order risk, and only about ₹18.4k of cash (enough for roughly 4 shares), stay out and revisit if price holds the ₹3,536 support with a confirmed reversal.

fundamental.thesis: Netweb Technologies builds high-performance computing systems, AI servers and private-cloud hardware in India, so it is a hardware and infrastructure maker rather than a labour-based IT services firm; the sector card's warning that AI deflates services revenue fits it poorly, and AI capex demand is more likely a tailwind. Growth is clearly very strong but hard to measure precisely. Q1 FY27 revenue was about ₹714 cr (+174.5% YoY) with PAT of ₹85 cr (+196.5%), and yfinance shows Q2 FY27 at about ₹1,091 cr revenue and ₹137 cr PAT. However, the extracted H1 FY27 figures (₹2,143 cr revenue, 19.7% PAT margin) do not reconcile with these quarters and come from an OCR-corrupted filing, so the exact Q2 growth rate and margin step-up are unverified; EBITDA margin also eased from 14.9% to 12.2–13.0% across FY26. Valuation is expensive on any yardstick: trailing P/E is 108.7x against an IT median of 22–30x, forward P/E is 60.7x and EV/EBITDA is 79.2x (I used EV/EBITDA as the primary measure for a hardware business), the stock ranks around P94–P96 against the broad market, and it sits at 74% of its 52-week range. Rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +11.8% over 90 days) support momentum but leave little room for any slip in lumpy, order-driven revenue.

drivers: H1FY27 results: no forward guidance; revenue +20.3% YoY (Project Work Services +29.1%) but PAT -5.5% as PAT margin fell to 6.58% from 8.24%
Cash flow from operations was negative at ₹-42.29 cr and capex was ₹160.04 cr; the ₹157.47 cr net cash cushions this
Market reaction was in-line: -2.2% on results day, then +0.4% over 2 days
No headlines for this stock in the last 7 days, so there is no recent news signal; Telecom sector flows were neutral

technical.setup: Range-bound midcap in a long-term downtrend (death-cross, price 14.5% below the 200-day average) bouncing toward its 50-day average resistance near 252 on a positive MACD turn, but with weak trend strength (ADX 18) and fading volume, so it reads as a relief rally into resistance rather than a confirmed reversal.

trader.reasoning: We don't own RailTel and none of the three analysts makes a case to start a position. Revenue grew 20% but profit fell 5.5% and margins keep shrinking, operating cash flow was negative, and valuation looks only fair; sentiment is flat with no fresh news. The chart shows a relief bounce into resistance near 252 inside a long-term downtrend with weak trend strength, and the market's current tendency for rallies to fade plus only about 18k of cash give no reason to fund an entry.

fundamental.thesis: RailTel is a state-owned railway telecom and IT-infrastructure company; its legacy telecom services business, which leases the railway fibre network, is now outgrown by lower-margin government project work, so the mobile-telecom sector card (ARPU, oligopoly) does not really apply. For H1 FY27, revenue grew 20.3% YoY to ₹2,039 cr from ₹1,695 cr, but PAT fell 5.5% to ₹134 cr and PAT margin compressed from 8.2% to 6.6%, continuing a slide from 8.9% in Q1 FY26 and 7.8% in 9M FY26. Revenue growth has also cooled from +33% to about +20%, and H1 PBT included ₹39 cr of exceptional items (vs ₹13 cr a year ago), so underlying profit quality is weaker than the headline. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA plus peer rank, not the card's 9-12x mobile-telecom band: 15.3x EV/EBITDA (P27 vs a broad-market median of 23.3x) and 32.6x trailing P/E (P46, near the median) grade it fair, and the forward P/E of 21.6x assumes an earnings recovery that the falling sell-side estimates (-3% over 90 days, 2 of 2 analysts at sell) do not yet support. The biggest risk is cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was -₹42 cr and free cash flow -₹202 cr, so growth is being bought with working capital and capex rather than producing cash.

HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is crude above $100 with a weakening rupee: marketing losses could return while the balance sheet is already stretched, with short-term borrowings up to ₹35,933 cr, a current ratio of 0.57, negative interest coverage and an ₹18,049 cr unrecognised LPG under-recovery.

Dalmia Bharat is a mid-sized Indian cement maker with 54.7 MTPA installed capacity across 12 states, expanding toward 67 MTPA, including the acquired Jaypee assets in Central India. Q2FY27 revenue, derived as H1 minus Q1 because the Q2 row is blank, was about ₹3,563 cr (+4.3% YoY, slowing from +10.7% in Q2FY26), and PAT was about ₹-201 cr after ₹339 cr of exceptional items; volume rose only 3%, EBITDA per tonne fell from ₹1,013 to ₹746, below the ₹900-1,100 healthy range, and management expects more fuel and Central India cost pressure in Q3. On the capital-intensive yardsticks of EV/EBITDA and EBITDA per tonne, I grade valuation fair: 12.3x EV/EBITDA is on depressed earnings, the 35.0x trailing P/E (Materials benchmark 12-22x) is distorted by one-offs, and the P19 EV/EBITDA and P15 P/B ranks are less useful because they compare against the broad market, not cement peers; the 15.7% position in the 52-week range offers some support, but this is not clearly cheap with FY EPS estimates cut about 19% in 30 days. The biggest risk is that fuel inflation and Central India dilution keep margins falling while capex of ₹3,200-3,400 cr continues, leading to further estimate cuts.

Neuland Laboratories makes APIs (active drug ingredients) and does contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) for global drugmakers. About 85% of revenue comes from exports, and it has 77 active US drug master files (DMFs) and a clean FDA record. It should benefit from the China+1 shift, and its export-led model is outside the US tariff on patented drugs. Results are lumpy, though: Q2FY27 revenue fell 11.4% YoY to ₹457 cr and PAT fell 47% to ₹51 cr. That came straight after an exceptional Q1 (revenue +116%, PAT ₹147 cr), and the PAT margin dropped from 22.7% to 11.2% between the two quarters. H1FY27 still looks strong, with revenue up 35% to ₹1,091 cr, PAT up 80% to ₹199 cr and cash flow from operations at 1.8x PAT. On valuation I used trailing and forward P/E and P/B, because the reported EV/EBITDA of 401x and debt/equity of 16x are almost certainly data errors for a company the filings show as net cash. At 60.6x trailing earnings (sector range 28–40x), 11.8x book and the P78 peer percentile, the stock is expensive. The 37.6x forward P/E already assumes the H1 growth rate carries on. The biggest risk is that the Q2 drop marks a pause in big customer orders rather than normal quarter-to-quarter swings, which would leave a premium valuation without the earnings to support it.

Brigade Enterprises is a Bengaluru-focused developer with residential projects plus a steady leasing and hospitality annuity business; its leasing segment earns a 67.5% margin and grew 1.3% YoY. H1FY27 consolidated revenue fell 13.2% YoY to ₹2,312 cr, mainly because real-estate segment revenue dropped 26.6% to ₹1,374 cr. PAT still rose 32.7% to ₹436 cr, lifting the PAT margin to 18.9%, and the implied Q2 alone (about ₹1,133 cr revenue, ₹219 cr PAT) was similar to Q1. The forward-looking metrics are thin: Q1FY27 bookings were ₹1,061 cr on 0.74 mn sq ft and collections were ₹1,856 cr, with no year-ago figure to show the trend. Cash conversion weakened to 0.42x CFO/PAT in H1, against 1.63x in Q1. Following the sector card, I judged valuation on bookings, collections and net debt, not P/E. On that basis, net debt/EBITDA of 2.1x, gross D/E of 0.79x, a forward P/E of 17x and a price at 53% of its 52-week range point to fair, not cheap, value. The snapshot's P/B of 30.5x and EV/EBITDA of 143.6x look like data errors, since net worth of about ₹7,155 cr against a ₹20,830 cr market cap implies P/B near 2.9x. The biggest risks are the revoked environmental clearance on a large Chennai project and a ₹860 cr landowner JDA dispute. Analysts also cut current-year EPS estimates by 6.1% in the last 30 days.

Jubilant Ingrevia is a mid-cap Indian chemicals maker with three segments: Specialty Chemicals, Nutrition (vitamin B3 and feed premixes) and Chemical Intermediates (acetyls). It is now adding CDMO capacity and has bought a 40% stake in ZettaOne, an electronics-materials business. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹1,394 cr, up 24% YoY and an all-time high, compared with low-single-digit growth through FY26 (+1.3% in Q1FY26, +5.0% for FY26). PAT rose 61% to ₹111 cr, and both PAT margin (8.0% vs 6.1–7.2% across FY26) and EBITDA margin (16.0% vs 13.6–14.8%) widened, but Q1FY27 is missing from the filings data, so the speed-up rests mainly on one quarter. I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, as the sector card says to for chemicals: at 18.1x it is far above the card's 5–8x mid-cycle range for commodity chemicals, though that range doesn't fully fit a specialty/CDMO mix; it is 22% below the broad-market median (P35), with trailing P/E of 34.6x at P48 and forward P/E of 22.3x, so I call it fair overall, not cheap. The main risks are muddy cash flow and earnings quality: finance costs jumped 85% YoY on acquisition-related borrowing, H1 FY26 earnings were weakly backed by cash (0.67x CFO/PAT, negative free cash flow), and analysts have trimmed next-year EPS estimates (−2.4% over 30 days, −3.7% over 90 days) even as they raised this year's.

Abbott India is the Indian listed arm of Abbott. It is a branded-formulations franchise focused on the domestic market (Thyronorm, Duphaston and other women's health, gastro and chronic-therapy brands), so it is in the sector card's 'safe template' group with no US-tariff exposure. The only reliable figures are full-year FY26: revenue of ₹6,929 cr (+8.1% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,552 cr (+9.7% YoY), with a 27.7% EBITDA margin and a stable 22.4% PAT margin. Cash conversion was good but not excellent (CFO/PAT 0.85x, FCF ₹1,278 cr). The Q1FY27 yfinance row does not add up (₹932 cr revenue against a ~₹1,730 cr quarterly run-rate, and a 46% PAT margin), so I ignored it. The Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-11-05 have not been extracted yet, which means I cannot read the current trend. On valuation, the trailing P/E of 35.8x sits inside the 28-40x pharma range and at P52 against peers, and EV/EBITDA is 28.1x (P62), so I grade it fair. The forward P/E of 28.8x points to expected earnings growth, and the stock trades at 8.4% of its 52-week range, a better entry point if the Q2 numbers hold up. The biggest risk is that the price slide reflects a weaker Q2 or growth slowing to mid-single digits, which this stale data cannot confirm or rule out. Two of the snapshot figures are almost certainly data errors and I ignored them: a dividend yield of 201% and debt/equity of 3.6 for a company that has historically had no debt (the second may be lease liabilities or a unit mismatch).

JSW Energy is a large private power producer with 15.1 GW of installed capacity, about 61% of it renewable, and a stated path to 30 GW by 2030 built on long-term power contracts. In Q2FY27, revenue rose 24.2% YoY to Rs 6,658 cr and PAT rose 38.5% to Rs 1,141 cr (17.1% margin, EBITDA margin 58.7%), but revenue growth has slowed from +78.6% in Q1FY26 and +59.8% in Q2FY26 as acquisitions enter the base, and Q1FY27 is missing from the trend table while the signals mix annual and quarterly rows. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive business, valuation grades expensive at 17.0x, backed by a trailing P/E of 45.1x against the 10-18x Utilities benchmark and a P/B of 3.29x against ROE of only 8.8%; the 'fair' broad-market peer read carries little weight because it has no tight industry peers. The biggest risk is that net leverage of 4.94x operational and 5.55x total, above the 4.5x target, must fund Rs 20,000 cr of FY27 capex while finance costs are up 14% and FY EPS estimates have been cut 3.1% over 90 days.

Godfrey Phillips is a mid-cap cigarette-led business (Marlboro licensee, plus Four Square and Red & White) with smaller retail and confectionery arms, so it is a tobacco cash business rather than a typical FMCG name. In Q2FY27, reported revenue rose 157.2% YoY to ₹4,198 cr while PAT fell 37.7% to ₹190 cr, after a 44.3% drop in Q1FY27. PAT margin fell from about 19% in H1 FY26 to 4.5%. The revenue jump does not match the yfinance quarterly rows (₹762–1,115 cr), so it most likely reflects a change in how revenue is reported, such as duties included in the top line, rather than real demand. The falling profit is the real signal: earnings have dropped for two quarters in a row. Using P/E plus earnings direction (tobacco does not deserve the 40–65× FMCG multiple), the stock looks fair at 23.2× trailing and 20.3× forward, about 34% below the broad-market median, but that discount is offset by falling profits and weak cash conversion (CFO/PAT of 0.34x in FY26). The biggest risk is that the profit drop reflects lasting tax or volume pressure on cigarettes and keeps going.

Devyani International is India's largest QSR franchisee by store count (2,255 stores), operating KFC, Pizza Hut, and Costa Coffee alongside own brands (Biryani By Kilo, Vaango), with a pending merger with Sapphire Foods targeting completion by end-FY27. Q1FY27 revenue grew 16.5% YoY to ₹1,580 cr — holding steady from prior-quarter acceleration — with PAT turning positive at ₹17 cr (1.1% margin) driven by KFC (+3.3% SSSG, +38% operating EBITDA YoY) and own brands, but badly offset by Pizza Hut India which collapsed -24.9% YoY with 13 net store closures and SSSG of -1.9% for a second consecutive negative quarter. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this Ind AS 116-heavy QSR (per sector card guidance on capital-intensive businesses), 21.06× sits near the broad-market peer median (P45), which might suggest fair, but reported EBITDA is inflated by ₹103.7 cr of lease-accounting treatment vs. operating EBITDA of only ₹151 cr (9.6% margin); the 103× forward P/E at P100 vs. all peers, a negative ROE of -2.6%, and D/E of 203× collectively signal the market is pricing in flawless execution of the Sapphire merger and a Pizza Hut turnaround management itself only expects in FY28. The biggest structural risk is that Pizza Hut's decline deepens post-merger integration while high finance costs (₹70 cr/quarter, 4.4% of revenue) keep PAT margins razor-thin, with sell-side EPS estimates already revised down -8.4% over 90 days despite a still-bullish analyst mix — a classic pre-derating pattern.

OneSource Specialty Pharma is a ₹18,258 cr mid-cap contract drug manufacturer with sterile capacity, and it has no close peers in the universe, so the peer comparison uses the broad market. The latest extract shows revenue of ₹965 cr, up 37.3% YoY, versus -1.6% in FY26, with EBITDA margin rising from 21.4% to 29.6% and PAT swinging from a ₹74 cr FY26 loss to ₹82 cr (8.5% margin), although the period comparison is not like-for-like: the 37.3% is tagged H1 FY27 while the company's headline attributes about 37% to Q2, and the +700.8% PAT growth comes off a very low base. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick because the business is capital-intensive and trailing P/E is unavailable, the stock looks expensive at 55.6x (+138% vs the broad-market median, P92); the 21.1x forward P/E implies roughly ₹865 cr of profit against ₹82 cr in the latest period, so it depends on a steep ramp that the filings here do not confirm. The biggest risk is that growth is not yet turning into cash, with H1 FCF of ₹-190 cr, CFO/PAT of -0.23x, 193 days of receivables and net debt/EBITDA of 5.14x, partly offset by the USFDA VAI classification that closed the Bengaluru sterile facility inspection.

Swan Corp is a midcap conglomerate whose main businesses are a shipyard (Swan Defence and Heavy Industries), an LNG/energy unit, textiles, chemicals and real estate. The desk tags it Materials, but the business does not fit any of the sector card's sub-industries, so the card's steel, cement and paints priors do not really apply. H1 FY27 revenue fell 12.4% YoY to ₹2,060 cr (from ₹2,352 cr), and EBITDA fell 27% to ₹101 cr, with margin down from 6.2% to 4.9%. Reported PAT of ₹530 cr (attributable ₹476 cr, up 3,001% YoY) comes almost entirely from a one-off current-tax credit of about ₹557 cr: before tax the company lost ₹27 cr, operating cash flow covered only 0.21× of PAT, and revenue growth has fallen from +11.4% to the negative range over the trend window. P/E (36.8×, in line with the market median) and EV/EBITDA (negative) are both distorted by the tax credit and the weak EBITDA, so I graded on P/B plus ROE: 1.42× book is low for the broad market (P9) but matches a 3% ROE, so fair, not cheap; on underlying earnings the stock is effectively loss-making, and the price sitting near its 52-week low (10% of range) looks more like a falling knife than value. The biggest risk is leverage: net debt is ₹1,471 cr, about 7.3× annualised EBITDA, and the promoter pledged more shares again in October and November 2026.

Blue Star is a leading Indian room air-conditioning (RAC) and electro-mechanical projects (EMP) company, positioned as a mid-tier premium brand competing with Voltas and Daikin in a structurally growing cooling market. In Q1FY27, revenue accelerated to +13.3% YoY (₹3,378 cr) driven by EMP (+15%) and unitary products (+12.7%), but PAT declined 15.1% YoY to ₹103 cr as EBITDA margin contracted sharply from 6.9% to 5.4% — the multi-quarter trajectory shows revenue growth re-accelerating while margins are compressing across all periods (PAT margin: 4.1% H1FY26 → 3.6% 9MFY26 → 4.2% FY26 → 3.0% Q1FY27), a structurally concerning divergence. At a trailing P/E of 62.75× against the Consumer Discretionary/Industrials sector median of ~28–45×, and with BLUESTARCO ranked at P80 in the broad market (78% premium to median P/E of 35.2×) alongside EV/EBITDA of 38.4× at a 65% premium to median, the stock is clearly expensive by both absolute and relative measures — the forward P/E at 40.4× does price in meaningful earnings recovery, but downward estimate revisions of -16.6% over 90 days suggest the market is still re-rating expectations lower. The biggest risk is that cost pressures (crude rising, competitive intensity in RAC) persist through FY27, making the earnings recovery priced into the forward multiple elusive and triggering a de-rating in a premium-multiple name where any guidance miss historically compresses valuation 25–40%.

Zensar is an RPG-group mid-tier IT services firm with two businesses, Digital Services and Cloud Infrastructure, and it has a net cash position of ₹326 cr. Revenue is growing a little faster: H1FY27 revenue was ₹3,094 cr, up 10.2% YoY, compared with +7.5% to +8.7% through FY26, and Cloud Infrastructure grew 12.3%. Profit is not keeping up. H1 PAT of ₹374 cr rose only 2.7%, and PAT margin fell to 12.1% from 13.6% in FY26. Some of that drop is a one-off ₹24.9 cr Labour Code provision, but excluding it margin is still only about 12.9%. Cash conversion has also weakened, with CFO/PAT at 0.73x and only ₹22 cr of free cash flow because capex took up 8% of revenue, which is unusually high for an IT services firm. On valuation it looks cheap: trailing P/E is 12.6x against an IT sector band of 22–30x, EV/EBITDA is 8.2x (P7 across the market), and forward P/E of 11.2x is below trailing. Treat that discount with care, though. The stock is near its 52-week low, analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by about 1.2–1.4% over 90 days, and the market may be pricing in AI-driven shrinkage of mid-tier IT revenue. The feed also has several conflicting numbers: the Q1 revenue figure differs between sources, the Q2FY26 row is off by a factor of 10, and D/E of 1.68 and a 351% dividend yield contradict the net-cash position. So read the cheap grade with somewhat less confidence.

Motherson Sumi Wiring India makes wiring harnesses for Indian carmakers and two-wheeler makers, and its sales depend mostly on Indian volumes, which makes it a direct play on India's premium-vehicle and EV mix. In the latest quarter extracted from filings (Q1 FY27), revenue grew +36.6% YoY to Rs 3,407 cr, up from +14.2% in Q1 FY26, but profit barely moved (+1.6% to Rs 145 cr). The profit margin fell from 6.0% to 4.3% and the operating margin from 10.2% to 7.7%. There are early signs of a recovery: the half-year filing implies Q2 profit of about Rs 224 cr (+35% YoY, which matches yfinance's Rs 223 cr), FY EPS estimates were raised +7.3% in the last 30 days, and the half-year revenue figure is labelled H1FY26 in the table but is probably H1 FY27. However, the 30 Oct Q2 FY27 results have not been extracted yet and the Q2 revenue figures conflict, so this recovery is unconfirmed. On valuation, I used EV/EBITDA and forward P/E, as the Auto card suggests for ancillaries: EV/EBITDA of 23.9x is at the peer median (P52), forward P/E of 25.1x sits inside the 18-30x Auto band, and trailing P/E of 40.2x is inflated by the margin dip. That makes the stock fair, not cheap, even though it trades near its 52-week low (11.5% of range) and has a 32.4% ROE. The 293% dividend yield and 10.79 debt/equity readings look like data-unit errors; the filings show net debt of only Rs 58 cr. The biggest risk is that margins stay squeezed by copper and commodity costs, rising crude and a new-plant ramp-up, so revenue keeps growing without profit following it.

Gabriel India is a domestic auto-component maker focused on shock absorbers and suspension. It leads in commercial vehicles (about 88% market share) and electric two-wheelers (about 57%), and about 40% of revenue comes from the replacement/aftermarket business. H1 FY27 revenue grew 20.8% YoY to Rs 2,673 cr, speeding up from +15.5% in Q1 FY27 and +14.8% for FY26. That leaves an implied Q2 of about Rs 1,247 cr. Profits are not keeping up: PBT grew only about 10% YoY, Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 8.7% against 9.6% in FY26, and the restatement after the demerger plus the new stakes in HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove make the growth partly inorganic and harder to compare year on year. Valuation is expensive however you measure it. The trailing P/E of 65x is far above the 18-28x auto band. EV/EBITDA of 36.9x (the main yardstick here, since the business is shifting toward a capital- and acquisition-heavy holding structure) and P/B of 12x sit in the top quartile of the broad market (P77 and P88). The forward P/E of 31.8x and recent FY EPS upgrades (+6.2% over 30 days) already assume strong earnings growth, while next-year estimates are edging down (-1.2% over 30 days). The biggest risk is that the deals take net debt from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 1,125 cr while operating cash flow falls 36% YoY, so any slip in integration or margins hits a stock priced for perfection.

Zydus Wellness is a mid-cap consumer wellness company (brands include Glucon-D, Complan, Sugar Free, Nycil and Everyuth). It has recently grown through debt-funded acquisitions: Naturell in India and Comfort Click in the UK for GBP 239 million. The latest extracted figures are stale and look inconsistent. The table labelled FY26 shows revenue of ₹396 cr (+46.2% YoY) and PAT of ₹20 cr (-43.2% YoY), but FY25 shows ₹2,709 cr. That suggests a mix of standalone and consolidated figures, or a quarter labelled as a full year. Even so, the direction is clear: EBITDA margin fell from 18.4% to 12.0% and PAT margin from 14.8% to 5.0%, while finance costs rose 718%. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-11-03 are not yet in the data. Using P/E as the yardstick, as the FMCG sector card does, valuation is expensive. Trailing P/E is 81.7x against a sector norm of 40–65x, EV/EBITDA is 38.5x (80th percentile, where 100 = most expensive), and ROE is only 3.4%. The forward P/E of 28.9x assumes a sharp earnings recovery, yet analysts cut their current-year EPS estimate by 21% in the last 30 days. Price is at 74% of the 52-week range, so the upside looks limited.

Narayana Hrudayalaya runs a large chain of affordable multi-specialty and cardiac hospitals in India and also owns a hospital business in the UK, which makes it a mid-sized hospital operator that grows by adding beds and raising occupancy and revenue per bed. PAT is the cleanest figure we have: Q2FY27 PAT was ₹301 cr, up 16.7% YoY (EPS ₹14.82 vs ₹12.72), faster than Q1FY27's +5.4%. Revenue figures disagree with each other, though: the filings table shows ₹2,896 cr (+73.6% YoY) while yfinance shows ₹1,627 cr, and the prior-year comparison rows look mis-scaled. Margins are clearly falling either way (operating margin down about 500 bps to 19.5%, H1 EBITDA margin 20.1% vs 25.0%), and strong cash conversion (H1 CFO/PAT 1.91x, FCF ₹594 cr) is the main support. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-heavy hospital chain, the stock trades at 25.4x, which is at or below where Indian hospital peers usually trade. Trailing P/E is 46.9x, but forward P/E of 26.6x implies earnings growth ahead, and the stock sits at 36% of its 52-week range, so fair overall. The biggest risk is that margins keep shrinking while debt stays high (D/E about 1.2x) and analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 3.7% over 30 days even though almost all of them rate it a buy.

FSN E-Commerce (Nykaa) is India's leading online-plus-offline beauty platform with 65 million customers and 338 stores, plus a smaller Fashion arm that is still scaling. In Q2FY27 consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to ₹3,006 cr and PAT rose 207% to ₹101 cr. Revenue growth has held steady at 27-29% for three quarters (+26.7%, +29%, +28%), and EBITDA margin has widened from 7.2% to 8.5% to 8.7%, against 6.8% a year ago. The key business metrics also look healthy: GMV is up 30%, Beauty EBITDA up 51% and House of Nykaa NSV up 36%, while Fashion's EBITDA margin is barely positive at 0.2%. For a platform business I judged valuation on EV/sales, EV/EBITDA and whether unit economics keep improving, not on trailing P/E. At about 8.5x sales and 106x EV/EBITDA (98th percentile of the market, forward P/E 112x at the 100th percentile), with the stock near the top of its 52-week range, the price already assumes years of margin gains, so I grade it expensive. The biggest risk is valuation, not execution: these names can drop 25-40% on a single growth or margin miss, and that risk is higher with no explicit FY27 guidance plus fresh spending on Nykaa NOW quick-commerce and the Simply Nam acquisition.

Schaeffler India is a precision components manufacturer (bearings, transmission systems, clutch parts) for automotive and industrial customers, leveraging its German parent's technology IP and commanding ~79% of revenue from the Mobility segment with a quality premium over domestic-only ancillaries. H1 2026 showed revenue growth of +18.1% YoY to ₹5,346 cr and PAT growth of +19.1% to ₹642 cr, with EBITDA margin expanding from 19.6% to 20.1% across the tracked periods — an accelerating trajectory, though CFO/PAT of 0.61× is borderline weak and the ₹547 cr dividend paid against only ₹389 cr CFO raises a capital-allocation flag. Trailing P/E of 53.77× is nearly 2× the auto ancillary sector median of 18–28× and sits at P72 in the broad market; EV/EBITDA of 34.46× likewise approaches the upper end of even the capital-goods range (28–45×), making the stock expensive on both primary metrics — the forward P/E of 41.53× confirms growth is already priced in. The biggest risk is the premium valuation built on an uninterrupted growth story, which offers no margin of safety if growth decelerates due to auto-sector cyclicality, rising crude input costs, ongoing subsidiary losses (KRSV PAT −₹32 cr H1), or EV disruption of traditional drivetrain demand.

Birlasoft is a mid-cap IT services company with about 11,100 staff, a shrinking base of 209 active clients and heavy reliance on its largest accounts (top 5 are 44.2% of revenue). Rupee revenue growth improved from -3.0% in H1 FY26 to +6.6% in Q2 FY27 and PAT rose 37.5% to about Rs 160 cr (11.3% margin; the table's Rs 142 cr revenue and Rs 16 cr PAT look like unit errors), but constant-currency revenue fell 1.6% and EBITDA margin slipped from 16.0% to 15.2%, so currency and possibly non-operating items appear to be flattering the headline trend. Using P/E and EV/EBITDA as the yardstick, the stock looks cheap at 13.8x trailing earnings against a 22-30x IT benchmark and at 6.1x EV/EBITDA, near its 52-week low, although the peer ranks are against the broad market rather than IT companies, and the 3.42 debt/equity and 231% dividend yield look like data errors and were not relied on. The biggest risk is that this is a value trap: H1 order wins rose 15% to $285M but Q2 new wins were only $47M, and falling client numbers plus AI price deflation could keep underlying growth negative.

Indus Towers rents mobile tower space to telecom operators, with about 2.7 lakh towers and 1.63 tenants per tower in the latest KPI data. Revenue growth slowed from +7.9% in Q3 FY26 to +4.6% in Q1 FY27 and +4.0% (₹8,516 cr) in Q2 FY27, while PAT growth went from +0.5% to -2.5% (₹1,793 cr), leaving H1 PAT down 1.6% at ₹3,519 cr; I treated the row labelled Q2FY26 as Q2 FY27 because H1 less Q1 revenue is exactly ₹8,516 cr, but the same subtraction gives PAT of ₹1,773 cr and the 55.3% H1 EBITDA margin sits above both quarters (53.6% and 54.4%), so the margin figures are only approximate. On EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for capital-intensive businesses, 8.12× is below its 9-12× range, which is written for mobile operators rather than tower companies, so I grade the stock cheap, helped by a 15.29× trailing P/E and H1 free cash flow of ₹4,332 cr, though the bottom-quartile peer ranks are against the broad market rather than true peers and slowing growth justifies part of the discount. The biggest risk is a major customer under AGR-related stress that is paying only monthly billings, which has already kept ₹198 cr of revenue unrecognised in H1, while the 13.31× forward P/E assumes roughly 15% EPS growth even as PAT falls and estimates are being cut (FY EPS -1.4% over 90 days); leverage is also unclear, because the reported 2.33× net debt/EBITDA does not reconcile with debt of about ₹21,000 cr implied by the 53% debt/equity, or roughly 1.1× annualised EBITDA.

Hindustan Zinc is India's dominant integrated zinc-lead-silver miner (Vedanta Group subsidiary) with near-monopoly status in domestic mined zinc and structural cost advantages that produce world-class EBITDA margins of 62.4% — a level no domestic peer can match. H1FY27 revenue surged 76.7% YoY to ₹28,840 cr (accelerating sharply from -4.4% in Q1FY26), PAT grew 143.4% YoY to ₹11,881 cr, and PAT margin expanded to 41.2% from 29.9% — a five-period trajectory of simultaneously accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins driven primarily by elevated zinc and silver commodity prices, with cash quality strong (CFO/PAT 1.12×). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive commodity miner, the stock trades at 10.59× — P13 among 473 peers and a 54.6% discount to the broad-market EV/EBITDA median — with trailing P/E of 17.46× squarely inside the Materials sector range (12–22×), grading cheap on peer-relative metrics, though 10.59× sits above the 5–8× typical mid-cycle range for base-metals cyclicals, signalling that some commodity-cycle-peak risk remains unpriced. The thesis is materially constrained by an unresolved ED/FEMA investigation (search and seizure June 2026, no regulatory communication as of the October 2026 filing) and SEBI observations on related party transaction disclosures — governance headwinds typical of Vedanta Group that can trigger a de-rating independent of commodity fundamentals, and are weighted heavily under the midcap governance overlay.

Aarti Industries is a mid-cap Indian specialty chemicals maker (benzene-based intermediates for agrochem, pharma and polymers), a cyclical business that stands to gain from China+1 sourcing shifts. Profit is recovering from a low base: H1 FY27 PAT more than doubled (+117.5%) to ₹324 cr, and Q2 FY27 PAT of about ₹170 cr on revenue of about ₹2,631 cr puts revenue up roughly 26% YoY (vs ₹2,086 cr in Q2 FY26) and the PAT margin at about 6.5%, up from 4.7% in FY26. The revenue figures in the filings disagree with each other (the H1 total of ₹6,065 cr does not match the two quarters added together), so the reported +41% to +60% revenue growth rates are not reliable; the PAT figures do add up. Using EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for chemical cyclicals, the stock trades at 19.4x, well above the sector card's mid-cycle norm of 5–8x, and 42x trailing P/E is above the 12–22x Materials range; ROE is only 7.2% against 2.95x book, and the price sits at 80% of its 52-week range, so it looks expensive even though the forward P/E of 24x and sell-side upgrades (+5.2% over 30 days) already assume strong earnings growth.

Jaiprakash Power Ventures is a midcap private power producer (thermal plus the Vishnu Prayag hydro plant) whose former promoter group, Jaiprakash Associates, was taken over by Adani Enterprises through insolvency in March 2026; it does not fit the regulated-return model the Utilities sector card describes. The last quarter extracted from the official filings, Q1 FY27, shows revenue up 12.2% YoY to ₹1,776 cr and PAT up 68.5% to ₹469 cr. That jump follows a weak FY26 (revenue +1.9%, PAT -44.6%) and is distorted by a one-time ₹108 cr net tax benefit and a ₹194 cr coal-mine surrender provision. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 19 Oct are not yet in the trend table, and the unverified yfinance figures (PAT ₹33 cr) hint at a sharp seasonal or underlying drop, so the 'accelerating' trajectory label should not be trusted. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-heavy business, 11.4x (P16 vs the broad market) and P/B of 1.23x look reasonable, but trailing P/E of 22.9x is above the 10–18x utilities band, so overall it is fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is roughly ₹2,000 cr of disputed claims (UPPCL ₹473 cr, AP sand-mining notices ₹857 cr, ICICI recompense ₹570 cr, a ~₹124 cr JAL guarantee), about 18% of market cap and none provided for, made worse by the CFO and Company Secretary both leaving on 30 Sep 2026.

Tata Consumer Products is India's second-largest branded foods-and-beverages company, with leading positions in tea (Tata Tea, Tetley) and salt (Tata Salt), supplemented by an inorganic expansion into nutrition and adjacent FMCG via Capital Foods, Soulfull, and Organic India acquisitions. Q1FY27 revenue grew +11.9% YoY to ₹5,349 cr — a meaningful deceleration from +15.0% in Q3FY26 — though PAT surged +28.8% YoY to ₹427 cr (margin 8.0% vs 7.0% a year ago), powered by lower tea input costs and gross-margin expansion from 40.1% to 42.7%; volume growth in the India business was ~13%, solid but to be weighed against the sector card's caution on >10% volume claims. At a trailing P/E of 60.51× — at the upper bound of the FMCG benchmark range of 40–60× and ranked P78 among broad-market peers — the stock screens as expensive even near its 52-week low; however, a forward P/E of 41.78× (31% below trailing) signals the market is pricing in a meaningful earnings step-up from acquisition integration and tea-cost tailwinds. The principal risk is sustained revenue growth deceleration toward sub-10% alongside a reported Debt/Equity of 12.16 (reflecting heavy acquisition financing), which leaves the stock highly exposed to multiple compression if earnings delivery disappoints or high-rate conditions pressure interest coverage.

JBM Auto combines a components business (Q2FY27 revenue about Rs 1,037 cr, +24.7% YoY) with a fast-growing electric bus business (about Rs 548 cr, +21.8% YoY, 24% reported market share and 578 buses delivered in the quarter). Reported revenue growth has accelerated from +8.6% in Q2FY26 to +16.2% in Q3FY26 and +21.1% to Rs 1,656 cr in Q2FY27, with PAT up 12.5% to Rs 59 cr, but PAT margin has slipped from 3.9% to 3.6% to 3.5%; Q1FY27 and FY26 data are missing, and the table's Q2FY26 revenue and PAT imply lower growth of about +17.7% and +7.3%, so the acceleration is less certain than it looks. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive business, valuation is expensive at 24.0x for a 12.2% EBITDA margin, even though that is only P52 against a broad-market peer set rather than close auto peers; trailing P/E of 64.8x is well above the 18-30x OEM range, P/B of 12.7x is P89, and forward P/E of 31.0x assumes earnings roughly double. The biggest risk is that growth keeps needing debt-funded capital while thin margins and weak cash generation (H1FY27 operating cash flow Rs 143 cr, free cash flow Rs 14 cr, net debt Rs 2,732 cr) leave little room for error; the 14.0% dividend yield looks like a data error and was ignored, and the '2.7x H1 revenue' debt figure is wrong because Rs 2,732 cr is about 0.9x H1 revenue.

GMDCLTD is a Gujarat state-owned miner whose main business is lignite. Mining brings in nearly all its revenue (FY26 mining revenue ₹2,508 cr out of ₹2,653 cr total), and the loss-making power segment adds the rest. In Q2FY27, revenue from the official filing rose 71.2% YoY to ₹903 cr, faster than +23.8% in Q1FY27. Reported PAT fell 63.3% to ₹171 cr, but that is because Q2FY26 included a one-time ₹474 cr GST credit; without it, PAT grew about 27%. The PAT margin is 18.9%, close to Q1's 18.0% and well below FY26's 36% (which was inflated by the one-off). The quarter was strongly cash-backed: operating cash flow was 3.9x PAT and free cash flow ₹376 cr. Because this is a capital-heavy commodity miner, the right measure is EV/EBITDA, and the reported 43.9x is far above the 5–8x mid-cycle norm for cyclicals. However, that figure, the 163% dividend yield and the 4.47 debt/equity do not fit with Q1 EBITDA of ₹267 cr and the low liabilities in the segment data, so I treat them as unreliable. On the more dependable cross-check, trailing P/E of 20.6x is at the top of the 12–22x Materials range and P/B of 2.78x with 14.2% ROE is not cheap. Forward P/E (22.0x) is above trailing, which means earnings are expected to fall, so the grade is fair, not cheap, even though the stock ranks low on P/E against the broad market. The biggest risk is that the 71% revenue jump does not match the yfinance figure (₹538 cr), and it brought only modest underlying profit growth while margins shrank.

The Ramco Cements is a mid-sized, South India-focused cement maker. The sector card describes the industry as consolidating, with UltraTech and Adani holding about 45% of capacity, which leaves smaller players like Ramco competing on price. Revenue growth has picked up, from -1.0% YoY in Q1FY26 to +9.6% in Q1FY27 and +10.0% in Q2FY27 (Rs 2,466 cr). Profit has gone the other way: Q2FY27 PAT fell 48.6% YoY to Rs 38 cr, a margin of just 1.6% versus 3.3% a year ago. EBITDA margin slid from 19.4% to 14.1% and EBITDA per tonne fell from Rs 981 to Rs 651 between Q1FY26 and Q3FY26, well below the Rs 900–1,100 band the sector card calls healthy. Q2FY27 profit also includes a Rs 4.8 cr exceptional gain and leaves out about Rs 8.6 cr of disputed mineral land tax, so underlying earnings are weaker than reported. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-heavy cement; my verdict is expensive. At 17.1x EV/EBITDA, 30.1x trailing P/E (above the 12–22x Materials range) and 2.6x book for only a 9% ROE, the stock is priced for a margin recovery the filings don't yet show. Forward P/E of 28.7x is barely below trailing. The broad-market peer ranks (P31 on EV/EBITDA) compare it with unrelated sectors, so I gave them little weight. The stock trades near its 52-week low, but that alone is not a reason to buy.

UPL is India's largest global agrochemical company, operating crop protection (UPL Corp), seeds (Advanta), and post-harvest segments across 130+ countries — a capital-intensive, leveraged cyclical recovering from a multi-year agrochem destocking cycle. Revenue has accelerated from a trough of +2% YoY in Q1FY26 to +10% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹10,181 cr consolidated); EBITDA grew 15% YoY to ₹1,500 cr with 180 bps contribution-margin expansion, and Q1FY27 PATMI was management's stated strongest in three years — a clear directional improvement from the -₹88 cr loss in Q1FY26, supported by broad-based platform growth (Advanta +26%, SUPERFORM +14%, UPL Corp +7%). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card guidance), UPL at 7.86× sits at P6 vs. 473 broad-market peers (67% discount to the 23.3× median) and at the mid-cycle floor for specialty chemicals (5–8× range); forward P/E of 12.65× is 46% below trailing 27.34×, signalling substantial earnings recovery priced in — the stock grades cheap on the appropriate metric. The primary risk is the combination of very high financial leverage (D/E flagged as extreme), NWC deteriorating sharply to 110 days (+24 days YoY from inventory build and FX translation), and persistent China-led price competition in agrochemicals — all amplified by rising crude input costs, INR weakness expanding USD-denominated debt service costs, and an ongoing RISK_OFF macro regime with FII net selling.

Allied Blenders and Distillers is a midcap Indian spirits maker, with a Rs 17,700 cr market value and thin margins on reported revenue that includes excise duty. Revenue growth has improved from -6.2% in FY26 to +1.9% in Q1 FY27 and +4.3% to Rs 3,903 cr in H1 FY27 (about +7% to Rs 2,094 cr in Q2, derived from the H1 and Q1 figures), but H1 PAT fell 3.6% to Rs 114 cr, the 2.9% PAT margin is slightly below H1 FY26's 3.2%, and the data shows neither volume growth nor a reliable gross margin trend. Using the sector card's FMCG P/E norm, cross-checked with broad-market EV/EBITDA and P/B ranks because there are no tight peers, the stock is expensive at 77.3x trailing P/E against 40-65x, with EV/EBITDA of 34.5x and P/B of 10.7x against 13.6% ROE; the 39.9x forward P/E implies EPS nearly doubling while near-term estimates are slipping about 1%. The biggest risk is a valuation de-rating if profit does not catch up with those expectations, and conviction is limited by data conflicts: implied Q2 PAT of Rs 65 cr vs Rs 71.5 cr on yfinance, a likely misstated 86% dividend yield, debt/equity of 68.25 that probably means 0.68x rather than 68x, and a price implied by the consensus upside (about Rs 694) that does not match the one implied by the 52-week position (about Rs 633).

scorecard.note: Forward returns measured from next-day open. Leak-free, post-cutoff. One regime so far — read as early signal, not verdict.

leaderboard.title: Technical pullback in uptrends
leaderboard.hypothesis: Technicals the right way round in a mean-reverting tape: buy the dip in a leader and give it time — a 10-session minimum hold and a 20-session cap keep the edge from being traded away in charges.

leaderboard.title: Engine as it is (control)
leaderboard.hypothesis: Production as it runs today: four agents per name, trader proposal, risk and tax checks, the entry gate. Entries on confirmation, exits on breakdowns.

leaderboard.title: Fundamental grades → rules
leaderboard.hypothesis: Strong growers that are not yet decelerating, held whole and long: the one filter with measured forward information (+2.5 pp at 60 sessions, +5.6 pp at 120 vs the equal-weight universe in the point-in-time study), alone — kept at target weight and re-qualified every 120 sessions.

leaderboard.title: Fundamental grades ∩ momentum, 200-day overlay
leaderboard.hypothesis: Our two independent signals (text and price) together: strong, non-decelerating growers that are also in a price uptrend; the most evidence-backed construct.

leaderboard.title: Macro + fundamental, sector rotation
leaderboard.hypothesis: Top-down sector timing adds to the bottom-up filter (strong, non-decelerating growers). Judged against b6_neutral — the same construction with every tilt at 1.0 — by more than the random band, plus the sector-call scorecard at one month (>= 60% hit, >= +1 pp per call, model months only); at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement, two quarters the floor.

leaderboard.title: AI-first, rebuilt (v2 briefing + guardrails)
leaderboard.hypothesis: With the right facts in front of it and the toxic actions fenced off, the AI's discretion adds value.

leaderboard.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
leaderboard.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

leaderboard.title: Quality factor (mechanical)
leaderboard.hypothesis: Quality from the filings alone — ROCE, margin, leverage, cash conversion, growth consistency, accruals — top 30, monthly, with the index overlay.

leaderboard.title: Fundamental grades → rules, old filter (a)
leaderboard.hypothesis: The pre-c1 Book 3 — moderate growers and the conviction leg, no acceleration leg — run live beside Book 3 to settle c1 vs (a) out of sample (the first 98-session replay had (a) ahead).

leaderboard.title: Pure 12-1 momentum rules
leaderboard.hypothesis: Book 4 without the fundamental filter: what price alone buys.

leaderboard.title: Multifactor (quality + momentum + low vol + value)
leaderboard.hypothesis: Equal-weighted z-score composite of quality, 12-1 momentum, low 60-day volatility and earnings yield — top 30, monthly, with the index overlay.

leaderboard.title: Book 6 bottom-up, neutral tilts (no model)
leaderboard.hypothesis: Book 6's construction with every sector tilt at 1.0, run live beside Book 6: the line the model tilt must beat by more than the random band (the bounds study of 26 Oct 2026 found no pack field beat it; the TWR line cannot judge the tilt, Book 6 − b6_neutral and the sector-call scorecard can).

books.title: Fundamental grades → rules
books.hypothesis: Strong growers that are not yet decelerating, held whole and long: the one filter with measured forward information (+2.5 pp at 60 sessions, +5.6 pp at 120 vs the equal-weight universe in the point-in-time study), alone — kept at target weight and re-qualified every 120 sessions.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

books.title: Fundamental grades ∩ momentum, 200-day overlay
books.hypothesis: Our two independent signals (text and price) together: strong, non-decelerating growers that are also in a price uptrend; the most evidence-backed construct.

rules.signal: monthly — first session on/after the month's last weekday (start date counts)
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); between signal dates the book holds except on a flip, when survivors are rebalanced (no entries or exits)
rules.universe: close > own 200-day SMA, 12-1 momentum known AND the shared fundamental filter (growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes))
rules.exit: rank > 60, close < 200-day SMA, fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high)
rules.entry: new entries wait until the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; holdings are never sold for timing

books.title: Technical pullback in uptrends
books.hypothesis: Technicals the right way round in a mean-reverting tape: buy the dip in a leader and give it time — a 10-session minimum hold and a 20-session cap keep the edge from being traded away in charges.

rules.universe: close > 200-day SMA and 12-1 momentum in the top 20% of names with momentum
rules.entry: 5-session return <= -4% or close < 20-day SMA; ranked by momentum (strongest first)
rules.hold: minimum 10 sessions from the fill (the stop still applies)
rules.exit: after the minimum hold, close >= 20-day SMA or 20 sessions held; -10% from the fill price at any time

books.title: Macro + fundamental, sector rotation
books.hypothesis: Top-down sector timing adds to the bottom-up filter (strong, non-decelerating growers). Judged against b6_neutral — the same construction with every tilt at 1.0 — by more than the random band, plus the sector-call scorecard at one month (>= 60% hit, >= +1 pp per call, model months only); at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement, two quarters the floor.

rules.signal: monthly — first session of the calendar month (or the first run after it); one sector_strategist call; none on other days or in a dry run
rules.tilt: per sector in [0.5, 2.0], clamped; sum of |change| per signal capped at 1.0; weights normalised to 1 over sectors with eligible names (neutral = equal share); fallback = the standing tilt (neutral at first)
rules.eligible: the shared fundamental filter: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes); ranked by revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.slots: 30 slots apportioned over the active sectors by largest remainder on w_s x 30 (sum = 30 exactly), with hysteresis: a sector's count changes only when its exact share moves > 0.5 slot from its current allocation; weight w_s / k_s each, capped at 2/30
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); rebalanced on the monthly signal date and on the flip
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions or exited in the last 20 sessions
rules.exit: fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high), or a tilt cut dropping k_s below the names held (lowest-ranked sold first); never on missing data, decelerating growth or timing
rules.rebalance: signal dates and the session the overlay flips; survivors outside +/-25% of target
rules.attribution: monthly Brinson vs the equal-weight universe + sector-call scorecard per signal at +5 / +21 / +63 sessions (the 1m row judges; leaderboard key book6_attribution)
rules.judge: Book 6 minus b6_neutral (the same construction, every tilt 1.0, zero LLM) must exceed the random band; scorecard at 1m >= 60% hit and >= +1 pp per call, over- and under-weights each above their own null (~45% / ~55%), model months only; at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement (two quarters is the floor)

books.hypothesis: Book 4 without the fundamental filter: what price alone buys.

rules.signal: monthly — first session on/after the month's last weekday (start date counts)
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); between signal dates the book holds except on a flip, when survivors are rebalanced (no entries or exits)

books.title: Quality factor (mechanical)

rules.signal: monthly — first session on/after the month's last weekday (start date counts)

rules.rank: composite z-score of the quality metrics (see docs/books.md), descending

books.title: Multifactor (quality + momentum + low vol + value)
books.hypothesis: Equal-weighted z-score composite of quality, 12-1 momentum, low 60-day volatility and earnings yield — top 30, monthly, with the index overlay.

rules.signal: monthly — first session on/after the month's last weekday (start date counts)

rules.rank: mean z of quality composite, 12-1 momentum, -60d volatility, earnings yield (value optional), descending

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
